stemBlocks.value: M = (1 2 −1 / 3 0 4), a 2 × 3 matrix, and N = (2 1 / −1 3 / 5 0), a 3 × 2 matrix. (a) State why M and N are conformable for the product MN. (b) Calculate MN. (c) State the order of MN.
Think first: Each row of M has three entries and each column of N has three entries, so the pairs match up perfectly.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p198-q10 from workbook page 198.

solutionSteps.instruction: Compare the number of columns of M with the number of rows of N.

contentBlocks.value: M is 2 × 3 and N is 3 × 2; both inner numbers are 3.

solutionSteps.instruction: Pair row 1 of M with each column of N.
Pair row 2 of M with each column of N.
Write the completed product and state its order.

strategyBlocks.value: Check the inner numbers agree, then form each of the four entries of MN by pairing one row of M with one column of N.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) M has 3 columns and N has 3 rows; since these numbers are equal, the product MN is defined  (b) MN = (−5 7 / 26 3)  (c) The order of MN is 2 × 2

whyThisWorks.value: Every entry of a product is a sum of products of matched pairs, so the row length of the first matrix must equal the column height of the second for the pairing to work. The entry in row i, column j of MN comes from row i of M and column j of N, which is a useful check if you lose your place. The 3s cancel out of the shape, leaving 2 × 2.
